items.title: $ONDS Walks like a duck , quacks like a duck .. by all means it must be a duck. The abnormally high failed to deliver events are hhighly sus
items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Walks like a duck , quacks like a duck .. by all means it must be a duck. The abnormally high failed to deliver events are hhighly suspect!!!. Under Reg SHO, a stock becomes a Threshold Security when FTDs persist for 5 consecutive settlement days, reaching ≥10,000 shares AND ≥0.5% of shares outstanding. ONDS reported: Aug 13: 10.59M FTDs Aug 14: 14.28M Aug 17: 20.95M Aug 18: 14.27M Aug 19: 17.38M Aug 20: 16.06M Aug 21: 10.16M That’s 7 consecutive reported settlement dates above 10M FTDs, with Aug. 17 alone representing roughly $193.6M in undelivered shares. And ONDS appeared on the Reg SHO Threshold List again in late September, including Sept. 25 and Sept. 30. The regulator’s own Reg SHO framework identified ONDS as having persistent delivery failures meeting the threshold criteria. FTDs alone don’t prove naked shorting—but this is documented evidence of massive, persistent failures to deliver that triggered the regulatory threshold and close-out framework.

items.title: $AMZN Amazon is pitching investors on an 8 billion sale-leaseback of its AI chips, per the FT. Thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips, al
items.content_excerpt: $AMZN Amazon is pitching investors on an 8 billion sale-leaseback of its AI chips, per the FT. Thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips, already running in a dozen-plus US data centers, would move into an outside-investor vehicle funded with debt. Amazon keeps up to a 10 percent equity stake and leases the chips back. One level down: this is GPUs as financial engineering. Meta already kept its Louisiana data center debt off the balance sheet through Blue Owl. The WSJ counted roughly 3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments across nine top tech names in August, mostly AI. Amazon gets cash and a cleaner balance sheet, and the fast-depreciating hardware is no longer its problem. The catch: the vehicle's higher borrowing costs come back to Amazon as higher lease payments. Tracking which hyperscaler does the next one.

items.title: Amazon will invest more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities that host its AI data centers through a new “Built Together” ini
items.content_excerpt: Amazon will invest more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities that host its AI data centers through a new “Built Together” initiative, as the company seeks to address local concerns surrounding rapid data-center expansion. The program, announced by AWS CEO Matt Garman, will fund free university education, workforce training and energy-efficiency improvements for schools and homes. Amazon also introduced a Data Center Commitment, promising that its facilities will not increase local electricity bills and that the company will publish annual data on energy and water consumption. Garman said Amazon will also stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies involved in its data-center projects, a practice that has become a point of contention among local opponents. The initiative comes as hyperscalers accelerate AI infrastructure investment and face scrutiny over electricity demand, water usage and grid upgrades. . $AMZN

items.title: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage conti
items.content_excerpt: Google has raised the price of its seven-month-old Pixel 10a by $100 to $599, citing higher memory costs as a persistent chip shortage continues to pressure the consumer electronics industry. The increase marks another example of rising component costs being passed on to smartphone buyers, even for older, lower-priced models. The Pixel 10a offers limited upgrades over the 2025 Pixel 9a and uses Google’s Tensor G4 processor, which was introduced two years ago. Meanwhile, Samsung has raised prices on most Galaxy S26 models by $100, while Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max also launched above their predecessors’ prices. Google’s newer Pixel 11 lineup started at $899, $100 above the previous generation, with the company adding more storage to entry-level configurations to offset part of the increase. The range reaches $1,899 for the base Pixel 11 Pro Fold, reflecting broader pressure on smartphone pricing from higher memory and component costs. $GOOGL $SSNLF $AAPL

items.title: $SOFI at $15.77 is dirt cheap IMO. Not because the stock is down. Because the numbers are starting to get ridiculous. Management is guiding
items.content_excerpt: $SOFI at $15.77 is dirt cheap IMO. Not because the stock is down. Because the numbers are starting to get ridiculous. Management is guiding for 32–35% revenue growth in 2026, ~$1.6B in adjusted EBITDA and around $0.60 in adjusted EPS. At today’s price, you’re paying roughly 26x 2026 adjusted earnings. Now look at what management expects beyond this year… At least 30% annual revenue growth through 2028. And 38–42% annual adjusted EPS growth. So I’m paying ~26x earnings for a company that believes earnings can compound around 40% annually over the next few years. Meanwhile members are still growing 35% YoY, products are growing 42%, and profitability keeps scaling. That’s why I think $SOFI is dirt cheap here. The stock got crushed. The business didn’t.

items.content_excerpt: $QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE ​ Rather than outsourcing to a giant like Fabrinet, QUBT made a distinct strategic choice to build its own highly specialized foundry in Tempe, Arizona. items.content_excerpt: $QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE COHR LITE & FN are the established giants capitalizing on the immediate AI data center boom. QUBT represents a radically different bet on what photonics can do next. Coherent and Lumentum are the picks & shovels of optical networking. They manufacture the raw components, InP lasers, VCSELs, & modulators—that shoot light across data centers. Their immediate catalyst is the AI boom; as massive GPU clusters require increasingly faster connections (like 800G & 1.6T transceivers), they are stepping in to provide the optical plumbing. For example, Coherent recently launched its PhotonLink platform specifically to integrate optics directly into AI hardware infrastructure.

items.title: $AGEN The IGCS poster delivered this morning. Three-year follow-up from the ovarian cohort of Agenus's C-800-01 trial: estimated overall
items.content_excerpt: $AGEN The IGCS poster delivered this morning. Three-year follow-up from the ovarian cohort of Agenus's C-800-01 trial: estimated overall survival 48%, unchanged from the two-year estimate. The survival curve flattened. Population context: median four prior lines of therapy, about three quarters platinum-resistant or refractory. In this setting conventional checkpoint immunotherapy has rarely produced lasting benefit. The subgroup math is the interesting part. Platinum-resistant/refractory (n=25): 47% three-year survival. Platinum-sensitive (n=10): 45%. Nearly identical. And 11 of the 44 treated patients, a quarter, are alive and off all therapy at last follow-up. Caveats stay on: Phase 1b, 35 efficacy-evaluable patients, no comparator arm. Tracking Monday's tape and whether the sell-side cluster re-rates off the data.

items.title: $AGEN One day someone will explain why botensilimab plus balstilimab (Bot/Bal) works at a very high level for about half the people who get
items.content_excerpt: $AGEN One day someone will explain why botensilimab plus balstilimab (Bot/Bal) works at a very high level for about half the people who get it. Noetik has been working on that question. If the reason is found, the same biology might show how to turn Bot/Bal into something stronger — a Bot/Bal-plus — that reaches the other half as well. Put yourself in the patient’s place. You have just been told you have one of the cancers this combination has activity in. The next years may be surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and other drugs, each with its own cost and damage. Would you want a shot at Bot/Bal at the start, not after everything else has failed? For roughly half of patients it may mean not having to go through the rest of that sequence. For the other half it may still mean a real chance at longer survival. That is a 50/50 the patient can feel. It is not a guarantee. It is a chance worth taking early.

To provide context on how this compares to the Agenus C-800-01 trial data: * Standard of Care: Patients with platinum-resistant disease receiving standard single-agent chemotherapy (e.g., paclitaxel, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, or topotecan) typically experience a median overall survival of about 12 months. * BOT+BAL Trial Results: The press release notes that in the C-800-01 trial, the median overall survival for the evaluable population was 14.8 months, with an estimated three-year survival rate of 48%.

Bullish Clinical Trial Agenus Reports 48% Estimated Three-Year Survival With BOT+BAL in Recurrent Ovarian Cancer at IGCS 2026 Red flags • BOT+BAL not FDA-approved; data are Phase 1b with small cohort (n=35 efficacy population) Agenus reported three-year follow-up data from the ovarian cancer cohort of its Phase 1b C-800-01 trial at IGCS 2026, with estimated three-year overall survival of 48% in recurrent ovarian cancer patients treated with botensilimab plus balstilimab. The survival estimate held steady from two years to three years, a plateau pattern suggesting durable benefit in a heavily pretreated population with a median of four prior lines of therapy, including platinum-resistant patients at 47% three-year survival. Objective response rate was 23% (8/35) with median overall survival of 14.8 months, and no new safety signals were observed. BOT and BAL remain investigational and are not FDA approved.

items.content_excerpt: Goldman Sachs bankers generated substantial fees from SpaceX’s successful June IPO, but the bank’s financial benefit from the company began years earlier. More than five years ago, Goldman helped wealthy clients invest in SpaceX when the aerospace company was valued at tens of billions of dollars. When SpaceX went public at a $1.77 trillion valuation, clients who sold shares realized significant gains, while Goldman collected hundreds of millions of dollars in related fees, according to people familiar with the matter. Goldman’s bankers received about $100 million as lead advisers on the SpaceX IPO, while the firm’s asset- and wealth-management business had previously provided clients with access to private SpaceX investment opportunities. Sources said Goldman partners were also able to invest alongside clients, potentially giving some current and former senior executives substantial gains. $GS $SPCX

The regulator’s own Reg SHO framework identified ONDS as having persistent delivery failures meeting the threshold criteria. FTDs alone don’t prove naked shorting—but this is documented evidence of massive, persistent failures to deliver that triggered the regulatory threshold and close-out framework.

$QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE ​ Rather than outsourcing to a giant like Fabrinet, QUBT made a distinct strategic choice to build its own highly specialized foundry in Tempe, Arizona. This foundry is dedicated to TFLN. TFLN is rapidly emerging as a superior material for chip-scale optical integration because it controls light at incredibly high speeds with minimal energy loss. By owning the fab, QUBT controls its supply chain for its quantum machines and can also act as a boutique manufacturer for outside customers.

$QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE COHR & LITE use photonics merely to move data between classical chips, QUBT is using photonics to actually compute the data. The Dirac-3S uses the physical properties of light to natively solve optimization math. They are pushing optics beyond just being a networking cable and turning it into the processor itself

$QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE COHR LITE & FN are the established giants capitalizing on the immediate AI data center boom. QUBT represents a radically different bet on what photonics can do next. Coherent and Lumentum are the picks & shovels of optical networking. They manufacture the raw components, InP lasers, VCSELs, & modulators—that shoot light across data centers. Their immediate catalyst is the AI boom; as massive GPU clusters require increasingly faster connections (like 800G & 1.6T transceivers), they are stepping in to provide the optical plumbing. For example, Coherent recently launched its PhotonLink platform specifically to integrate optics directly into AI hardware infrastructure.

$QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE photonics; replacing electrons moving through copper with photons moving through optical pathways. ​As silicon chips & data centers hit critical limits regarding heat generation, energy consumption, & data transfer speeds. Photonics offers a solution. It allows data to move faster, over longer distances, with virtually no heat & drastically less power.

$QUBT $COHR $FN $LITE $LYTE QUBT: The Specialized Optimizer (Photonics) ​Dirac-3S is an analog optimization machine, not a universal computer. It uses integrated photonics to natively map & solve combinatorial math. Finding the single most efficient outcome out of millions of variables.
